page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with no margin notes. Top: a two-line verse couplet. Then three poem headings, each followed by its stanza. Bottom: signature and catchword. The page number is at the top right.

main_text.p:
Ars bona vi magna non est mercabilis auri,
Illa sed in pigro parta labore venit.
main_text.head: XV. Laurentius Scheichius Grunbergensis.

p.i: Huc ergo Scheichi, & hinc tuam fer lauream,
Aptam: probis, & his unis, quos auream
Fas carpere illinc: improbis autem nefas.
At tu fuscae Scheichi vinculum comae
Amicè suscipe, quod pia dextra porrigit.

main_text.head: XVI. AEgidius Keil Eschuicensis.
main_text.p:
UBi malignus nodus est,
Quaerendus asper cuneus est:
Nam cunei vis est maxima.
Ingenium si sit plumbeum,
Ut haereat fixissimis
Radicibus scientia
Animo tandem, unus cuneus est,
Et alter, Diligentia,
Et continuata Motio
Cerebri, & crebra lectio.
His, AEgidi, cuneis tibi
Adeptus es hanc lauream.
Sic perge, habebis auream.
main_text.head: XVII. Bernhardus Breslerus[?] Marpurgensis.
main_text.p:
HUc ades, ursinum qui praefers nomine robur,
Hac tegat ornatum laurus odora caput.
Laurea frontis honos, tali quae Jaspide fulget,
Cum natura usus perficit artis opus.

page.notes: The second line of the opening couplet reads "im pigro" in the scan; this is most likely "in" and is kept as the letters appear. The poet's name in XVII is read as "Breslerus" and is uncertain. The stanzas are printed in verse lines with broken lines marked by line breaks. The heading lines are printed in larger roman type and are treated as level 3 headings. The initial letters L, U and H are large woodcut initials and are joined to the first word.
